| [CLAIM-580](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-580.md) v2 | The transition threshold is stable under error in the resource function: if an estimate of the requirement is within ε of the true one at every configuration, the estimated threshold is within ε of the true one, and an underestimate anywhere can only lower it while an overestimate can only raise it | The assistant's own proposition, offered at the owner's invitation on 2026-11-05. The threshold of [CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) is the least, over admissible paths, of each path's peak requirement, and both the peak and the least move by at most the largest error in the requirement. So a planner who knows each configuration's cost to within ε knows a transition's threshold to within ε, and its reconfiguration slack to within 2ε. The error is also one-sided in a useful way: overestimating only raises the threshold, and underestimating anywhere can only lower it, possibly by opening a cheaper path that does not exist. It is the zero-dimensional case of the stability of sublevel-set persistence that Mirth et al. use. With several resources the same argument bounds the set of sufficient budgets coordinate by coordinate. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [CLAIM-581](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-581.md) v4 | Under peak-capacity costs on reversible moves, the transition threshold between configurations is an extended pseudo-ultrametric, so identifying configurations reachable within a budget is an equivalence relation at every budget and the identifications nest into one tree as the budget grows; under additive costs the threshold is only an extended pseudometric, budgeted identification need not be transitive, and no such tree exists | The assistant's own proposition, filed on 2026-11-05 at the owner's invitation to contribute. Take configurations joined by reversible moves, each move with a peak requirement, and let d(x, y) be the least, over paths, of the largest requirement on the path ([CLAIM-571](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md)'s threshold, identities free). Concatenating a path from x to y with one from y to z has peak max(d(x, y), d(y, z)), so d(x, z) ≤ max(d(x, y), d(y, z)): d is an extended pseudo-ultrametric (distinct states joined at no cost are at distance 0, unjoined ones at ∞; it is an ultrametric only when every pair of distinct states is separated by a positive cost). Hence at each budget b, "x and y can be turned into one another within b" is an equivalence relation, its classes are the components of the budget-b move graph, and as b grows the classes only merge, forming one dendrogram, the merge tree of zero-dimensional sublevel persistence (Mirth et al.). Under additive costs d is a metric and budgeted identification is intransitive in general. So which resource semantics governs a system decides whether "the same thing, within budget" sorts its configurations into a hierarchy of kinds at all. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |

| [CLAIM-699](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-699.md) v2 | Where the reward used in RL post-training is also available as a verifier at test time, the RL model's single-sample gain is a cheaper route to what base sampling filtered by that verifier reaches at matched compute, and should not exceed it at large budgets; RL's distinctive value lies where recognition at test time is unavailable or costly, so the substitutability of training and search is fixed by the cost of recognition | The assistant's hypothesis, offered at the end of the filing of 2026-11-15 and filed at the owner's request. | [CLAIM-704](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-704.md) v3 | In an idealized overloaded review process (homogeneous challenges arriving at rate λ, one service time s = 1/μ each with μ < λ, a common window F ≥ s, no batch corrections), the order of review decides whose right to challenge still prevents anything: first-come review in the limit resolves none in time, while an order that serves only challenges it can still finish in time reaches the largest possible share, μ/λ, once F ≥ s + 1/λ; under insufficient review capacity, scheduling distributes preventive rights | The assistant's, offered at step 12 of the filing of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-16 ("file your ideas as well"). This claim says which orders reach the bound and which fall to zero: first-come review, the default and the one that looks fair, falls to zero because after t* = (F − s)μ/(λ − μ) everything it resolves is already too late; serving the newest first, or the oldest challenge whose window is still open, reaches μ/λ. So under overload no order preserves everyone's right, and choosing one distributes which rights stay preventive. Checked by simulation. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-705](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-705.md) v6 | When an institution produces challengeable decisions faster than its corrective process can resolve them, the formal right to challenge stays with everyone while its preventive effect cannot: if valid challenges arrive at rate λ and are resolved at rate μ < λ, at most a share μ/λ can ever be resolved in time, whatever the order of review, and under first-come review none filed after a finite time is | A's, from A35 §3 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-15): "an action-producing system can exceed the corrective throughput of the institutions intended to constrain it", with A's worked numbers (10,000 decisions a day, 1% needing correction, 50 appeals resolved a day) and its analogy to queueing stability. With A's numbers t* is ten days. Checked by simulation. It is [TERM-085](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md)'s deadline applied to a stream of cases. The wording is A's; the derivation is the filer's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-724](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-724.md) | Against a challenged party who can act on the means of correction, correctability is a robust quantity, the chance that a corrective policy reaches its objective against every strategy in a declared class of opposition, and it depends on who moves first, since a corrector that must commit before seeing the opposition can do strictly worse than one that responds to it; judged against the opposition the procedural rules permit, failure shows the institution inadequate, and failure owed to opposition outside them shows a wrong by the opponent as well | A's, first stated A76 VIII.4 of the exchange "Assess Depp Heard Abuse" (2026-11-16) as "Adversarially robust correctability", refined A81 §3 (2026-11-17) with claimant–institution policies and the split Σ_permitted ⊆ Σ_physically available; A90 IX restates it. | [CLAIM-777](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-777.md) | If ideas arrive at rate λ, are coded by one first-come coder at rate κ > λ, and are restated once per unit of time while they wait, an idea's expected drift before it is coded is σ²/(κ − λ) in mean square for features copied with error and (c − x₀)·ln(1/a)/(κ − λ + ln(1/a)) in mean for contracted ones, so drift tracks the ratio of arrival to anchoring hyperbolically and grows without bound as the ratio reaches one; coding at a fixed occurrence caps it at that many restatements' worth | [CLAIM-186](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md)'s arrival against anchoring, as a queue. Under Poisson arrivals, exponential coding times and one restatement per unit of waiting time, the drift an idea accrues before it is coded follows from the mean sojourn 1/(κ − λ) and [CLAIM-773](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-773.md)'s rates. | [CLAIM-878](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-878.md) | Under a budget set each period to the last period's peak spending, a capability stays funded exactly as long as every period contains a mobilization at its cost, whether a use, a drill, a false alarm or a cancelled dispatch, so dispatching it provisionally to every report keeps it funded far longer than dispatching it only on confirmation of need | A corollary of [CLAIM-577](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-577.md), found in running [LEAD-080](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-080.md)'s study ([CASE-315](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-315.md)). Under spend-matching the next budget is this period's peak, so a capability costing B* to mobilize stays affordable exactly as long as every period has something that mobilizes it, and its first period with nothing loses it for good. If q_t is the chance that period t has nothing, the chance of losing it within n periods is 1 − ∏(1 − q_t). Whatever mobilizes counts: a use, a drill, a false alarm or a provisional dispatch ([TERM-109](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-109.md)) cancelled minutes later. So the dispatch policy decides how long the capability survives the rule. Sent provisionally to six reports a month, a heavy rescue squad is quiet in a month with chance e^(−6) and was still funded after nine years in 80 % of the study's runs; sent only on confirmation it was lost in every run within months. [CLAIM-561](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-561.md) says a high cancellation rate does not show waste; under this rule the cancellations are also what keeps the capability funded. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-879](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-879.md) | In a queueing model whose overseer keeps the same authority, information and reviewers at every speed, making the acting institution's actions irreversible sooner lowers the share of objectionable actions stopped in time gradually and from before the timing condition fails at the means; at the settings run, precommitted limits win back the share they foresee and automatic suspension the share detected in time, each delaying only what it holds, while a pause wins back capacity only by giving up the speed, and wins back none when speed also multiplies the volume of actions | The assistant's, from carrying out [LEAD-068](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-068.md), the simulation arm of [CASE-285](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-285.md). Over 20 seeds: at ten times the speed the share of objectionable actions stopped before irreversibility fell from 0.994 to 0.396, already 0.711 at five times, where A23 §3's condition still holds at the means; with volume multiplied too, to 0.043. In the fast arm, limits restored their coverage of the gap keeping 0.92 to 0.99 of the speed's benefit, suspension at most the 0.54 detected in time keeping 0.91 to 0.99, and pauses restored half the gap for a third of the benefit and none of it under the volume reading. It is a demonstration in an invented model: it shows that speed alone can separate an institution's action from its correction ([CLAIM-462](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md)) and that a step which holds what it catches and delays nothing else can carry intervention opportunity without impedance ([CLAIM-706](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-706.md)), not that any institution works so. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-880](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-880.md) | In the coupled meaning–influence model with declared demands, the frustration of satisfiable demands follows the allocation of influence when search and information are held fixed, but a captured allocation acts as a fixed weighting rule, so the model shows the governance-induced kind caused by allocation without showing conferral dynamics causing what no fixed weighting would | [LEAD-081](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-081.md)'s experiment, run as [CASE-317](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-317.md). With the update map and the gradients the same under every rule, scoring components by agreement with the update made captures influence and leaves a satisfiable demand unmet on 0.95 of steps; scoring each by its own demand's residual gives 0.05. Step size, curvature and noise move the first rule less, and lower it only by stopping capture. So frustration follows the allocation, as [CLAIM-500](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-500.md) and [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) expect. But the captured state is a fixed weighting, a fixed uniform weighting fails about as often, and a fixed weighting chosen in hindsight does as well as the second rule. The model separates allocation from search and information. It does not separate conferral dynamics from a fixed weighting rule, which [CLAIM-500](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-500.md)'s defeater counts as an optimizer mechanism. Whether that supports [CLAIM-500](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-500.md) or leaves its stronger form open is left to the owner as two readings. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

[QUESTION-114](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md) asked for the test: one cost model that prices the bugs, a filed argument and a LEGO bin with the same terms. A model with those terms, [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s, [CLAIM-761](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-761.md)'s per-demand budget and [CLAIM-760](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-760.md)'s parties does price all three, in [CASE-326](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-326.md), without adding a term for any of them. The four listed terms alone do not: the cockpit is carried by the price of work at the moment it is done, which they lack. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-921](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-921.md) | Where competence decays without funded maintenance and a capability is committed only when competent enough, a budget that follows observed use has a state in which the capability is never used or funded again whenever the base budget alone sustains competence below that level, any stretch without occasions long enough for competence to decay there reaches it whatever each use was paid, so at the same expected funding a rarer capability is lost sooner, while maintenance funded apart from use, at a level that sustains the threshold, has no such state | Found in running [LEAD-036](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-036.md)'s study ([CASE-343](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-343.md)) of A's model from [QUESTION-386](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-386.md). Competence k decays at rate δ and is rebuilt by maintenance bought from the budget above a holding cost h; the budget is a base B̄ plus η times observed use; and a capability is committed to an occasion only if k is at least k_lo. If the base alone sustains competence below k_lo, (β/δ)(B̄ − h) < k_lo, a capability that falls below k_lo is never committed, so never observed, so funded at the base, so never recovers. A stretch without occasions long enough for k to decay from its ceiling below k_lo reaches that state whatever earlier uses earned, so the chance of loss has a lower bound that rises as occasions grow rarer and does not depend on η: paying more per use does not make up for rarity. Funding maintenance apart from use at a level that sustains k_lo removes the state. In the study, at the same expected funding, the coupled rule lost the capability within thirty years in every run at one occasion in two and a half years and in 39 % at four a year, and the decoupled rule never did. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-922](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-922.md) | In a model with a home and a staging architecture and one capacity, the same intervention, admitting the staging architecture, creates reachability where the home configuration space is disconnected and only lowers the bottleneck budget where it is connected, while a budget or a reserve changes neither the bottleneck budget nor the least time, and a deadline shorter than every route through the staging architecture takes that remedy away | From the executed study [CASE-345](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-345.md), [LEAD-075](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-075.md)'s run of A's staging experiment. Admitting a staging architecture is one intervention; in the model it creates reachability when a crease constraint disconnects the home space, and when the home space is connected it lowers the bottleneck budget or does nothing, by the closed form B*(staging admitted) = min(B*(home), max(max(h0, h1) + s, h1 + β1/4)), derived and confirmed in 960 settings. A budget or a reserve never moves the bottleneck budget or the least time; it moves the capacity toward them. The staging route saves capacity and costs time (at least 2.58 against 1 in the base model), so at a deadline of 2 the architectural remedy is gone and a case reachable only through it becomes one reachable only with the reserve, or not in time. For [QUESTION-392](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-392.md): whether an intervention creates a capability or cheapens one is fixed here by the home architecture and the contingency's deadline, not by the kind of intervention. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
